arxiv-1501-00302.title: An Event-Driven Approach for Studying Gene Block Evolution in Bacteria
arxiv-1501-00302.creator: David C Ream, Asma R Bankapur, Iddo Friedberg
arxiv-1501-00302.description: Abstract Motivation: Gene blocks are genes co-located on the chromosome. In many cases, genes blocks are conserved between bacterial species, sometimes as operons, when genes are co-transcribed. The conservation is rarely absolute: gene loss, gain, duplication, block splitting, and block fusion are frequently observed.

arxiv-2101-10395.title: Representations of closed quadratic forms associated with Stieltjes and inverse Stieltjes holomorphic families of linear relations
arxiv-2101-10395.creator: Yu.M. Arlinskiĭ, S. Hassi
arxiv-2101-10395.description: Abstract . In this paper holomorphic families of linear relations which belong to the Stieltjes or inverse Stieltjes class are studied. It is shown that in their domain of holomorphy ℂ ∖ ℝ + {\mathbb{C}}\setminus{\mathbb{R}}_{+} the values of Stieltjes and inverse Stieltjes families are, up to a rotation, maximal sectorial.

arxiv-2301-03520.title: Classifying weak phase retrieval Thanks: The first author was supported by NSF DMS 1609760
arxiv-2301-03520.creator: P. G. Casazza, F. Akrami
arxiv-2301-03520.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by P. G. Casazza, F. Akrami. We will give several surprising equivalences and consequences of weak phase retrieval. These results give a complete understanding of the difference between weak phase retrieval and phase retrieval. We also answer two longstanding open problems on weak phase retrieval: (1) We show that the families of weak phase retrievable frames { x i } i = 1 m \{x_{i}\}_{i=1}^{m} in ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} are not dense in the family of m m -element sets of vectors in ℝ n

arxiv-2308-06993.title: Implications of supermassive neutron star for the form of equation of state of hybrid stars
arxiv-2308-06993.creator: Hongyi Sun, Dehua Wen
arxiv-2308-06993.description: Abstract The observations of PSR J0952-0607 ( M = 2.35 − 0.17 + 0.17 ​ M ⊙ M=2.35^{+0.17}_{-0.17}~M_{\odot} ) and the second object in GW190814 event ( M = 2.59 − 0.09 + 0.08 ​ M ⊙ M=2.59^{+0.08}_{-0.09}~M_{\odot} ) indicate the possible existence of supermassive neutron stars.

arxiv-2310-01843.title: Selective Feature Adapter for Dense Vision Transformers
arxiv-2310-01843.creator: Xueqing Deng, Qi Fan, Xiaojie Jin, Linjie Yang, Peng Wang
arxiv-2310-01843.description: Abstract Fine-tuning pre-trained transformer models, e.g., Swin Transformer ( Liu et al. 2022 ) , are successful in numerous downstream for dense prediction vision tasks. However, one major issue is the cost/storage of their huge amount of parameters, which becomes increasingly challenging to handle with the growing amount of vision tasks.

arxiv-2312-12294.title: Hard Lefschetz theorem and Hodge–Riemann relations for convex valuations Thanks: AB was supported by DFG grant BE 2484/10-1. Thanks: JK was supported by DFG grant BE 2484/5-2 and by Charles University grant PRIMUS/24/SCI/009. Thanks: TW was supported by DFG grant WA 3510/3-1.
arxiv-2312-12294.creator: Andreas Bernig, Jan Kotrbatý, Thomas Wannerer
arxiv-2312-12294.description: Abstract . The algebra of smooth translation-invariant valuations on convex bodies, introduced by S. Alesker in the early 2000s, was in part proved and in part conjectured to satisfy properties formally analogous to those of the cohomology ring of a compact Kähler manifold: Poincaré duality, the hard Lefschetz theorem, and the Hodge–Riemann relations.

arxiv-2403-11294.title: Probing multi-particle bunching from intermittency analysis in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
arxiv-2403-11294.creator: Valeria Zelina Reyna Ortiz, Maciej Rybczyński, Zbigniew Włodarczyk
arxiv-2403-11294.description: Abstract It has been demonstrated that factorial moments analysis in dependence from the size of phase-space cells (when the latter is decreased but is still considerably large), exhibits sensitivity to particle bunching within a system situated in the two-dimensional cell.

arxiv-2407-12952.title: Latent Diffusion for Medical Image Segmentation: End to end learning for fast sampling and accuracy
arxiv-2407-12952.creator: Fahim Ahmed Zaman, Mathews Jacob, Amanda Chang, Kan Liu, Milan Sonka, Xiaodong Wu
arxiv-2407-12952.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Fahim Ahmed Zaman, Mathews Jacob, Amanda Chang, Kan Liu, Milan Sonka, Xiaodong Wu. Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DPMs) suffer from inefficient inference due to their slow sampling and high memory consumption, which limits their applicability to various medical imaging applications. In this work, we propose a novel conditional diffusion modeling framework (LDSeg) for medical image segmentation, utilizing the learned inherent low-dimensional latent shape manifolds of the target objects and the embeddings of the source image with an end-to-end framework.

arxiv-2502-02694.title: Love numbers of black p-branes: fine tuning, Love symmetries, and their geometrization
arxiv-2502-02694.creator: Mikhail M. Ivanov
arxiv-2502-02694.description: Abstract We compute scalar static response coefficients (Love numbers) of non-dilatonic black p p -brane solutions in higher dimensional supergravity. This calculation revels a fine-tuning behavior similar to that of higher dimensional black holes, which we explain by “hidden” near-zone Love symmetries. In general, these symmetries act on equations for perturbations but they are not background isometries.

arxiv-2502-16387.title: Simultaneous Swap Regret Minimization via KL-Calibration
arxiv-2502-16387.creator: Haipeng Luo, Spandan Senapati, Vatsal Sharan
arxiv-2502-16387.description: Abstract Calibration is a fundamental concept that aims at ensuring the reliability of probabilistic predictions by aligning them with real-world outcomes. There is a surge of studies on new calibration measures that are easier to optimize compared to the classical ℓ 1 \ell_{1} -Calibration while still having strong implications for downstream applications.

arxiv-2507-13305.title: Boosting Team Modeling through Tempo-Relational Representation Learning
arxiv-2507-13305.creator: Vincenzo Marco De Luca 1,a, Giovanna Varni 1,b, Andrea Passerini 1,c
arxiv-2507-13305.description: Abstract Abstract Team modeling remains a fundamental challenge at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and the Social Sciences. Social Science research emphasizes the need to jointly model dynamics and relations, while practical applications demand unified models capable of inferring multiple team constructs simultaneously, providing interpretable insights and actionable recommendations to enhance team performance.

arxiv-2510-19181.title: Interpretable Question Answering with Knowledge Graphs
arxiv-2510-19181.creator: Kartikeya Aneja, Manasvi Srivastava, Subhayan Das, Nagender Aneja
arxiv-2510-19181.description: Abstract This paper presents a question answering system that operates exclusively on a knowledge graph retrieval without relying on retrieval augmented generation (RAG) with large language models (LLMs). Instead, a small paraphraser model is used to paraphrase the entity relationship edges retrieved from querying the knowledge graph. The proposed pipeline is divided into two main stages.

arxiv-2601-05606.title: Conformity Dynamics in LLM Multi-Agent Systems: The Roles of Topology and Self–Social Weighting
arxiv-2601-05606.creator: Chen Han, Jin Tan, Bohan Yu, Wenzhen Zheng, Xijin Tang
arxiv-2601-05606.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly instantiated as interacting agents in multi-agent systems (MAS), where collective decisions emerge through social interaction rather than independent reasoning. A fundamental yet underexplored mechanism in this process is conformity, the tendency of agents to align their judgments with prevailing group opinions.

arxiv-2601-11247.title: Observation of known APNs
arxiv-2601-11247.creator: Valérie Gillot, Philippe Langevin
arxiv-2601-11247.description: Abstract . We present new invariants, apn -extendibility criterion and a backtracking approach to identify several numerical facts supporting the conjecture that the set of 6-bit apn functions is limited to 14 ccz -classes. 1. Introduction At the Finite Fields conference FQ9 in Dublin, K. A. Browning, J. F. Dillon, M. T. McQuistan, and A. J.

arxiv-2602-11811.title: On the numerical evaluation of the ‘exact’ Post-Newtonian parameters in Brans-Dicke and Entangled Relativity theories
arxiv-2602-11811.creator: Thomas Chehab, Olivier Minazzoli
arxiv-2602-11811.description: Abstract In context of Brans-Dicke scalar-tensor theories of gravity, it has recently been obtained that the post-Newtonian parameters should be generalized in the context of strongly gravitating bodies, and that its generalization—the so-called exact parameters —actually depends on the pressure and energy density of a considered celestial body.

arxiv-2606-13703.creator: Hans van Ditmarsch

This award supported the research activities three faculty in the University of New Hampshire Department of Physics and Astronomy: Dr. Chanda Prescod-Weinstein (PI), Dr. Per Berglund (Co-I), and Dr. David Mattingly (Co-I). europmc-pmc2777001.title: Genevestigator v3: a reference expression database for the meta-analysis of transcriptomes.
europmc-pmc2777001.creator: Hruz T, Laule O, Szabo G, Wessendorp F, Bleuler S, Oertle L, Widmayer P, Gruissem W, Zimmermann P.
europmc-pmc2777001.description: The Web-based software tool Genevestigator provides powerful tools for biologists to explore gene expression across a wide variety of biological contexts. Its first releases, however, were limited by the scaling ability of the system architecture, multiorganism data storage and...

jewish-encyclopedia-1906-marburg-10391.title: MARBURG (Jewish Encyclopedia article)
jewish-encyclopedia-1906-marburg-10391.creator: Gotthard Deutsch, L. Munk, S. Mühsam

plos-pone-0001740.title: Architecture of an Antagonistic Tree/Fungus Network: The Asymmetric Influence of Past Evolutionary History
plos-pone-0001740.creator: Corinne Vacher, Dominique Piou, Marie-Laure Desprez-Loustau
plos-pone-0001740.description: PLOS ONE research article. Compartmentalization and nestedness are common patterns in ecological networks. The aim of this study was to elucidate some of the processes shaping these patterns in a well resolved network of host/pathogen interactions. Based on a long-term (1972–2005) survey of forest health a

pmc-10532019.title: Properties of Plant Virus Protein Encoded by the 5′-Proximal Gene of Tetra-Cistron Movement Block
pmc-10532019.creator: Denis A Chergintsev, Anna D Solovieva, Anastasia K Atabekova, Alexander A Lezzhov, Sergei A Golyshev, Sergey Y Morozov, Andrey G Solovyev, Hee-Jae Cha
pmc-10532019.description: To move from cell to cell through plasmodesmata, many plant viruses require the concerted action of two or more movement proteins (MPs) encoded by transport gene modules of virus genomes. A tetra-cistron movement block (TCMB) is a newly discovered transport module comprising four genes.

pmc-11324877.title: Mitochondrial network reorganization and transient expansion during oligodendrocyte generation
pmc-11324877.creator: Xhoela Bame, Robert A. Hill
pmc-11324877.description: Oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) give rise to myelinating oligodendrocytes of the brain. This process persists throughout life and is essential for recovery from neurodegeneration. To better understand the cellular checkpoints that occur during oligodendrogenesis, we determined the mitochondrial distribution and morphometrics across the oligodendrocyte lineage in mouse and human cerebral cortex.

pmc-11409341.title: Road to Recovery: protocol for a mixed-methods prospective cohort study evaluating the impact of a new model of substance use care in a Canadian setting
pmc-11409341.creator: Brittany B Dennis, Jeanette Bowles, Cheyenne Johnson, Travis De Wolfe, Erika Mundel, Danya Fast, Jade Boyd, Mathew Fleury, Paxton Bach, Nadia Fairbairn, M Eugenia Socías, Lianping Ti, Kanna Hayashi, Kora DeBeck, M J Milloy, Guy Felicella, Jeffrey Morgan, Cameron R Eekhoudt, Kimberlyn McGrail, Lindse
pmc-11409341.description: AbstractIntroductionThe Road to Recovery (R2R) Initiative is an innovative model of substance use care that seeks to increase treatment capacity by creating approximately 100 new addiction treatment beds to provide on-demand addiction care in Vancouver, British Columbia, for patients with substance use disorders.

pmc-11416837.title: Flapless Guided Dental Implant Surgery in a Systemically Compromised Patient: A Case Report
pmc-11416837.creator: Pamela Campos, Rafael Manfro, Gustavo Coura, Márcio de Carvalho Formiga
pmc-11416837.description: The use of surgical guides in implant treatment offers several advantages, including reduced surgery time, flapless procedures, and enhanced precision and reliability in implant placement. By utilizing tomography and scanning technologies, a patient’s complete anatomical structure can be transferred into software in three spatial planes.

pmc-11474419.title: Patterns of Migration Following Dementia Diagnosis
pmc-11474419.creator: Momotazur Rahman, Bishnu Bahadur Thapa, Christopher Santostefano, Pedro Gozalo, Ulrike Muench, Cyrus M. Kosar, Hyesung Oh, Elizabeth White, Vincent Mor
pmc-11474419.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Key PointsQuestionIs a dementia diagnosis associated with the likelihood and nature of migration compared with other major illnesses?FindingsIn this cohort study of more than 1 million Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries, individuals with a diagnosis of dementia were almost twice as likely to migrate to another county or state compared with those with diagnoses of myocardial infarction, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, or colon cancer.

pmc-11476923.title: Capillary Refill Time as a Part of Routine Physical Examination in Critically Ill Patients Undergoing Vasoactive Therapy: A Prospective Study
pmc-11476923.creator: Fabian Wesołek, Zbigniew Putowski, Wiktoria Staniszewska, Robert Latacz, Łukasz J Krzych, Giorgio Berlot
pmc-11476923.description: Background/Objectives: In critically ill patients, achieving a mean arterial pressure (MAP) of 65 mmHg is a recommended resuscitation goal to ensure proper tissue oxygenation. Unfortunately, some patients do not benefit from providing such a value, suggesting that other indices are needed for better hemodynamic assessment.

pmc-11513161.title: Neurofeedback: potential for abuse and regulatory frameworks in the United States
pmc-11513161.creator: Fiona Furnari, Haesoo Park, Gideon Yaffe, Michelle Hampson
pmc-11513161.description: Neurofeedback is a brain-training technique that continues to develop via ongoing innovations, and that has broadening potential impact. Once confined primarily to clinical and research settings, it is increasingly being used in the general population. Such development raises concerns about the current regulatory mechanisms and their adequacy in protecting patterns of economic and political decision-making from the novel technology.

pmc-11519075.title: Influence of Light-Curing Time and Increment Thickness on the Properties of Bulk Fill Composite Resins With Distinct Application Systems
pmc-11519075.creator: Carlos Rocha Gomes Torres, Taiana Paola Prado, Daniele Mara da Silva Ávila, Cesar Rogério Pucci, Alessandra Bühler Borges
pmc-11519075.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The objective of this study was to evaluate the influence of light-curing time and increment thickness on the microhardness and degree of conversion (DC) of bulk fill composite resins with different application systems. Translucency parameter (TP) was also measured. Specimens of resin composites were prepared in a circular matrix using a single increment with different thicknesses (2, 4, and 6 mm) and light-cured with distinct times (10, 20, and 40 s).

pmc-11643969.title: Preparation and Evaluation of a Combination of Chelating Agents for the Removal of Inhaled Uranium
pmc-11643969.creator: Lintao Li, Runtian Li, Ruohan Guo, Shuang Guo, Xuan Qiao, Xinru Wu, Peng Han, Yunbo Sun, Xiaoxia Zhu, Zhuona Wu, Hui Gan, Zhiyun Meng, Guifang Dou, Ruolan Gu, Shuchen Liu, Massimiliano F Peana
pmc-11643969.description: Inhalation of aerosolized uranium is recognized as a principal mode of exposure, posing significant risks of damage to the lungs, kidneys, and other vital organs. To enhance nuclide elimination from the body, chelating agents are employed; however, single-component chelators often exhibit limited spectral activity and low effectiveness, resulting in toxicologically relevant concentrations.

pmc-11666494.title: The cerebral metabolic mechanism of group computer magnanimous therapy based on magnetic resonance spectroscopy: effects on improving magnanimous-enterprising levels of lung cancer patients
pmc-11666494.creator: Qianyu Liu, Qihui Ma, Qingfeng Sun, Xuewei Huang
pmc-11666494.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThis study aims to evaluate the effects of group computer magnanimous therapy (GCMT) on magnanimous-enterprising levels and brain metabolic changes in patients with advanced lung cancer.MethodsIn this multicenter, randomized controlled trial, 47 participants diagnosed with advanced stage (III or IV) lung cancer were randomly assigned to either the GCMT group (GCMTG, n = 31) or the control group (CTRLG, n = 16).

pmc-11676239.title: Objective Approach for Titration of Continuous Positive Airway Pressure in Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea Using Daytime Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Titration Based on Respiratory Movement Regularity
pmc-11676239.creator: Naoto Burioka, Yuki Hirayama, Masahiro Endo, Masayoshi Oguri, Miyako Takata, Tomoyuki Ikeuchi, Akira Yamasaki, Sukhwinder Singh Sohal
pmc-11676239.description: Background/Objectives: Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is used to treat patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and has proven clinical efficacy for this condition. However, the objective method to determine the appropriate CPAP level for treatment is still unclear. Patients with OSA typically exhibit irregular respiratory efforts due to obstruction or narrowing of the upper airway during sleep.

pmc-11691665.title: HOW DO FAMILY RELATIONSHIP PATTERNS IMPACT CAREGIVING BURDEN IN ADULT CHILD CAREGIVERS?
pmc-11691665.creator: Jodi Heys, Jessica Strong
pmc-11691665.description: Living with dementia is not isolated to the person with the diagnosis. Family and friends play an integral role in providing support, advocacy, love, and informal care for a person with dementia. Spouses and adult child caregivers have a unique relationship with the person with dementia (PWD), and often report a different subjective experience of caregiving (Rigby, et al, 2019).

pmc-12473930.title: Integrating Microorganism-Based Therapy and Emerging Biotechnology in the Treatment of Intracranial Central Nervous System Diseases
pmc-12473930.creator: Zifan Li, Shihua Yang, Lida Su, Yoshiyuki Kubo
pmc-12473930.description: The development of drug delivery systems for the treatment of intracranial central nervous system (CNS) diseases remains one of the most intractable medical problems in modern society, owing to the special physiological structure of the brain, including the existence of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), the CNS’s immune privilege, and its high complexity and vulnerability.

pmc-12618232.title: Activation of kainate receptor GluK2–Neto2 complex
pmc-12618232.creator: Shanti Pal Gangwar, Maria V. Yelshanskaya, Laura Y. Yen, Thomas P. Newton, Alexander I. Sobolevsky
pmc-12618232.description: Kainate receptors (KARs) are tetrameric, ligand-gated ion channels of the ionotropic glutamate receptor family that mediate excitatory neurotransmission and modulate neuronal circuits and synaptic plasticity during development of the central nervous system. KARs are implicated in psychiatric and neurological diseases and represent a target of therapeutic intervention.

pmc-12651374.title: Research Progress on Signalling Pathways Related to Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury in Children
pmc-12651374.creator: Zhenkun Zhang, Meijun Sheng, Yiyao Bao, Chao Tang
pmc-12651374.description: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is a prevalent and life-threatening complication in critically ill children, contributing to high mortality rates (up to 30%) and long-term renal dysfunction in pediatric intensive care units. This review synthesizes recent advances in the signalling pathways underlying SA-AKI, emphasizing pediatric-specific mechanisms, biomarkers, and therapeutic targets.

pmc-12827544.title: GutMicrobiotAware: an international exploratory survey on awareness and understanding of the gut microbiota
pmc-12827544.creator: Enriqueta Garcia-Gutierrez, Sara Arbulu, Charlotte Oliver, Sandeep Kumar, Sarita A. Dam, Babette Jakobi, Vincenzo Pennone, Fabiana A. Hoffmann Sarda, Arghya Mukherjee, Paul D. Cotter
pmc-12827544.description: Over the past two decades, scientific understanding of the composition and function of the human gut microbiome has expanded substantially. The recent surge in human gut microbiota-related studies has unveiled the profound influence of the gut microbiota on host nutrition, health, and behavior, bridging biology, medicine, and ecology, among others.

pmc-12860026.title: High prevalence and underdiagnosis of osteoporosis in total hip arthroplasty candidates: a comprehensive assessment using bone mineral density, trabecular bone score, and bone turnover markers
pmc-12860026.creator: Shinichi Ueki, Takeshi Shoji, Takuma Yamasaki, Hiroyuki Morita, Yosuke Kozuma, Naoto Nakayama, Nobuo Adachi
pmc-12860026.description: BackgroundTotal hip arthroplasty (THA) effectively alleviates symptoms in individuals with hip osteoarthritis. However, some candidates may have undiagnosed osteoporosis, and bone mineral density (BMD) alone may not sufficiently reflect bone fragility. The trabecular bone score (TBS) and bone turnover markers (BTMs) provide additional information on bone quality and metabolism.

pmc-12976567.title: Research status and trend of lung cancer ablation therapy: a bibliometric analysis from 2002 to 2025
pmc-12976567.creator: Qingxu Zou, Dongyuan Qi, Xiangdong Huang, Zishu Zhang, Fengwu Lin
pmc-12976567.description: BackgroundLung cancer ablation treatment is to insert an antenna into the tumor under imaging guidance, resulting in tumor coagulation necrosis through extreme energy changes. It is one of the main local treatments for lung cancer and has become a prominent research area in recent years.

pmc-13306097.title: α-Synuclein-Targeted Immunotherapies in Parkinson’s Disease: In Silico, In Vitro and Clinical Perspectives
pmc-13306097.creator: Tatiane B. Santos, Tatiane de O. X. Machado, Pedro Henrique S. Rodrigues, Willamys S. Correa, Helena A. C. Kodel, Klebson S. Santos, Margarete Z. Gomes

pmc-13380929.title: Inhibition of VNN1-Induced ROS-Dependent NETs Formation Alleviates Lung Injury and Systemic Inflammation in Sepsis Mice
pmc-13380929.creator: Shishuai Meng, Xinyue Ma, Wei Yang, Mingyan Zhao
pmc-13380929.description: PurposeExcessive neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation worsens disease progression in sepsis. Vascular non-inflammatory molecule 1 (VNN1) is a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored protein. The present study investigated the mechanism of the role of VNN1 in NETs formation and sepsis.MethodsNeutrophils from mouse bone marrow were isolated for experiments and mRNA sequencing. A cecum ligation and puncture-induced sepsis mouse model was established.

pmc-13479630.title: Update to the management of recurrent urinary tract infections in women aged 16 years and older
pmc-13479630.creator: Leigh Sanyaolu, Haroon Ahmed, Miriam Santer, Sian Jones, Gail Hayward

pmc-13652473.title: Pregnancy after the Manchester–Fothergill procedure: a case report
pmc-13652473.creator: Zinat Ghanbari, Tahereh Eftekhar, Maryam Deldar, Hawraa Shbeeb, Shahla Pouyamoghadam, Marjan Ghaemi
pmc-13652473.description: Introduction and importance:Cervical elongation is commonly associated with uterine prolapse. The Manchester–Fothergill procedure offers a fertility-preserving surgical option for its correction. However, conception following this procedure is exceedingly rare, with an estimated incidence of 1 in 10 000.Case presentation:We present the case of a 35-year-old multiparous woman (G3P2L2) who conceived 18 months after undergoing the Manchester–Fothergill procedure for cervical elongation.
